properties.name: Bandilngan — Windjana Gorge Mini-Tunnel
properties.comment: To enter the famous gorge trail you walk through a small natural split-rock tunnel corridor. Instant cave vibe before a massive canyon filled with freshwater crocodiles.

properties.name: Cosy Corner Sea Caves
properties.comment: South of the car park, visible along the limestone cliffs of the beach.

properties.name: Calgardup Cave
properties.comment: Torches and helmets provided. Great boardwalks over seasonal water features. Contains a stream that trickles through year-round, carrying nutrients to tiny cave creatures. Also the information and booking centre for Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park adventure caves.

properties.name: C-96 Anomaly Cave Exterior
properties.comment: Cape Range has over 700 highly sensitive wild karst caves and is one of the most significant cave fauna areas on Earth. Home to Australia's only two troglobitic fish — the blind gudgeon and blind cave eel. Relict fauna from a much wetter past. Entry not permitted due to safety and protection of rare bats and troglobites.

properties.name: Cave Point
properties.location: Fitzgerald River National Park, Hopetoun / Bremer Bay
properties.comment: Incredible coastal viewing platform looking directly over a collapsed limestone and spongolite sea cave where the Southern Ocean crashes into the cliff base.

properties.name: Crystal Cave
properties.comment: Perth's only metropolitan tourist cave. Main tour requires a ticket. Surrounding paths show collapsed limestone karst depressions and historic stone infrastructure. Root mat communities harbour rare aquatic cave animals.

properties.name: Dimalurru — Tunnel Creek
properties.comment: WA's oldest cave system. A breathtaking 750m natural tunnel through 350-million-year-old Devonian reef limestone, up to 20m high and 15m wide. Stalactites, permanent pools, ghost bats, fruit bats and freshwater crocodiles inside. Roof collapsed near centre letting in daylight. Historic hideout of Bunuba leader Jandamarra, killed at the entrance in 1897. Aboriginal rock paintings on cave walls.

properties.name: Devil's Lair
properties.location: Witchcliffe area, south-west WA (closed archaeological site)
properties.comment: One of Australia's most significant archaeological sites. Stone and bone artefacts, intact campfire ash-beds and mammal bones show Aboriginal people occupied this cave about 50,000 years ago. Children's teeth indicate family groups used it. Stone tools confirm food preparation and camp activities. Closed to visitors to protect the site.

properties.name: Fern Pool & Circular Pool Caverns
properties.comment: Massive collapsed rock amphitheatres with overhanging ironstone ledges, hidden mossy grottos and small rock cavities. Scenic rather than deep subterranean.

properties.name: Giants Cave
properties.comment: Pitch black self-guided exploration. Entered via a spectacular collapsed doline almost 100m in diameter, plunging 86m into the earth. Vertical ladder climbs, boulder scrambles and tight squeezes through the Chimney. Hard hats and torches mandatory. One of the biggest and deepest caves on the Leeuwin-Naturaliste Ridge.

properties.name: Jewel Cave
properties.comment: WA's largest show cave. Named after the Jewel Casket formation in its lower section. Home to one of the longest straw stalactites in the world. Features lavish cave formations ranging from tiny crystal clusters to enormous flowstones that glow gold in artificial light.

properties.name: Lake Cave
properties.comment: Features a stunning Suspended Table formation hanging over a permanent crystal lake. One of the most impressive cave entrances in WA — at the bottom of a huge closed depression. The lake is formed by a stream flowing through the cave.

properties.name: Mammoth Cave
properties.comment: One of the south-west's biggest and most spectacular caves. Natural time capsule containing remains of long-extinct megafauna including Zygomaturus trilobus (hippo-sized marsupial), giant echidna Zaglossus hacketti (largest known monotreme), two species of extinct short-faced kangaroo, and thylacine remains. Enormous caverns thickly encrusted with beautiful speleothems.

properties.name: Mandu Mandu Gorge Rock Shelters
properties.comment: Easy walking trail through a dry ancient riverbed with shallow open-face limestone cave shelters in the sheer canyon walls visible from the path.

properties.name: Mimbi Caves
properties.location: Emanuel Range, east of Fitzroy Crossing
properties.access: 2WD to meeting point — 4WD track to site
properties.comment: Complex maze of deep limestone fissures and marine fossil walls. Inner sanctuaries require a guided Gooniyandi cultural tour. Outer karst portals visible from base tracks.

properties.name: Mulka's Cave
properties.comment: Iconic inland cave near Wave Rock. No deep caving gear needed. Notable for a vast collection of ancient Indigenous handprint art.

properties.name: Mullet Lake Sea Caves
properties.comment: Small limestone fractures and low-ceiling cave entries along coastal tracks east of Esperance. Best viewed from the exterior.

properties.name: Ngilgi Cave
properties.comment: The first cave in WA to be opened to tourists — enchanting visitors for over a century. Rich significance in the legends of the local Wardandi Aboriginal people. Features dazzling speleothems. Semi-guided tours available plus adventure tours into deeper sections.

properties.name: Stockyard Gully
properties.location: Stockyard Gully National Park, near Jurien Bay
properties.comment: A spectacular natural tunnel cave you can walk through — three registered caves in one system (Stockyard Tunnel 6E-1, Stockyard Bridge 6E-2, Stockyard Cave 6E-3). Part of a significant Eneabba karst area with numerous dolines and cave systems. Torch recommended. Similar experience to Tunnel Creek but in the mid-west.

properties.name: The Blowholes and Sea Tunnels
properties.comment: Easy paved walk along dramatic granite coastline. Look right down into coastal fractures where the ocean forces air and water through the rock chambers.
